summary: Defines an information model for PSAMP, listing the data items used to encode sampled packet data and details about the sampling process. It builds on the IPFIX information model and extends it for packet sampling reports.

eli5.summary: Reports need agreed words so everyone understands them. This note is the dictionary of terms for describing sampled network packets and how they were picked, adding to a dictionary that already existed.

questions: what is the psamp information model
how do psamp and ipfix relate
subtitle: The dictionary of data items a router uses to report which packets it sampled and how it picked them.

tldr.problem: Packet sampling needs a standard way to describe and export sampled packet data and the sampling process, and the existing IPFIX information model did not cover everything PSAMP Reports need.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 5477 defines extra Information Elements, starting at ID 301, for selectors, sampling and hash settings, timestamps, packet sections and statistics. PSAMP Reports are exported with IPFIX.
tldr.outcome: Exporters and Collectors share one vocabulary for sampled packets. It is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no replacement.

today: RFC 5477 is a Proposed Standard published in March 2009, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It remains the definition of the PSAMP Information Elements in the metadata we have.

sections.title: Why PSAMP Needs Its Own Information Model
sections.content:
Packet Sampling (PSAMP) selects subsets of packets using filtering and sampling techniques and reports on them. RFC 5477 is one of four PSAMP documents: RFC 5474 gives the framework, RFC 5475 describes the selection techniques, RFC 5476 specifies how to export packet information from an Exporting Process to a Collecting Process, and this document defines the information and data model.

The PSAMP protocol is based on IPFIX, and a PSAMP Report can be seen as a special IPFIX Data Record: a Flow containing only a single packet. The IPFIX information model (RFC 5102) is therefore the basis, but PSAMP needs properties it cannot express. RFC 5477 lists only the Information Elements that IPFIX does not already describe.

Packet error information such as drops or malformed packets is not covered. If it is needed, the Information Elements can be requested from IANA.
sections.eli5: A school already has a form for describing a whole class trip. This note adds the extra boxes needed to describe a single student picked at random from the crowd, and how they were picked.

sections.title: How the Elements Are Defined
sections.content:
The Information Elements follow the property rules in Sections 2.1 to 2.3 of RFC 5102, and they MUST be built from its abstract data types and semantics. The data types are not repeated here, and their encoding is in the IPFIX protocol (RFC 5101). The RFC strongly recommends defining the optional units property for every element where it applies.

Elements SHOULD NOT be overloaded with several meanings. An element written with one selection method in mind is not limited to it and MAY be used for other methods in the future. Even though other elements may allow the selection method to be inferred, a separate selectorAlgorithm element exists so it can serve as scope for Selector Report Interpretation.

Each element gets a unique ID, allocated under IANA control as an extension of the IPFIX model. The main body of Section 8 was generated from an XML document, which is attached as Appendix A. The body is normative and the appendix is informational.
sections.eli5: Every new word in the dictionary gets one job and its own number. Nobody is allowed to use one word to mean three different things.

sections.title: Describing How Packets Were Selected
sections.content:
The element selectorAlgorithm (ID 304) says which selection method a Selection Process applies. The methods come from RFC 5475 and each has parameter elements that fully specify it.

Systematic count-based sampling uses samplingPacketInterval (packets sampled consecutively) and samplingPacketSpace (packets skipped between intervals). Systematic time-based sampling uses samplingTimeInterval and samplingTimeSpace, both in microseconds. Random n-out-of-N sampling uses samplingSize and samplingPopulation. Uniform probabilistic sampling uses samplingProbability, a value between 0 and 1 that is equal for every packet.

Property match filtering has no agreed parameters, and three hash-based filtering methods are defined, using BOB, IPSX and CRC. New method identifiers go in an IANA registry under Expert Review, and each new method MUST have a unique value with its parameters and Options Template reporting clearly specified.
sections.eli5: Picking packets is like picking kids for a game. You can take every tenth kid, pick by lucky draw, or pick by name tag. This part has the words to say which way you used.

sections.title: Hash Settings
sections.content:
Hash-based selection runs a hash function over part of each packet and selects the packet if the result falls in a chosen range. The hash elements describe this setup, and their parameters are explained further in RFC 5475.

hashIPPayloadOffset and hashIPPayloadSize say which part of the IP payload is hashed. hashOutputRangeMin and hashOutputRangeMax give the function's potential output range, while hashSelectedRangeMin and hashSelectedRangeMax give the range that causes selection. hashInitialiserValue is the starting value for the function, hashDigestOutput is a boolean saying whether the output is included in the report as a packet digest, and digestHashValue carries the digest itself.
sections.eli5: Hashing is like shaking a packet through a number machine and keeping it only if the number that falls out is in a lucky range. These words describe how the machine and the lucky range are set.

sections.title: Reporting Packets, Times and Statistics
sections.content:
Four timestamp elements (IDs 322 to 325) report the absolute observation time of a single packet in seconds, milliseconds, microseconds or nanoseconds.

Four packet data elements carry raw packet content as octet arrays that MUST NOT be padded. ipHeaderPacketSection starts at the IP header and ipPayloadPacketSection at the IP payload. For IPv6 the payload is everything after the 40-octet header, so extension headers count as payload. mplsLabelStackSection and mplsPayloadPacketSection carry the first n octets of the MPLS label stack and of the payload after it. The exported size may be limited by IPFIX.

The statistics elements report on the Metering Process. selectorIdTotalPktsObserved and selectorIdTotalPktsSelected count packets per selector. absoluteError and relativeError give the maximum possible error of a measured value. For an estimate from sampling, upperCILimit, lowerCILimit and confidenceLevel describe a confidence interval, and they should be disregarded unless all three are specified together. The identifier elements selectionSequenceId, selectorId and informationElementId tie reports to the selectors that produced them.
sections.eli5: Each report can say when the packet was seen, show a few bytes from it, and say how many packets were looked at in total and how sure the counting is.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The information model does not itself create security issues, but the attributes it defines may be sensitive for privacy or business reasons. Exporting header field values may make attacks possible for the receiver that would otherwise be possible only for direct observers of the flows.

The packet-section elements MUST target no more than the packet header, some subsequent bytes and encapsulating headers if present. Full packet capture of arbitrary streams is explicitly out of scope, citing RFC 2804. The protocol that carries the data MUST apply appropriate procedures for integrity and confidentiality, which are defined in the IPFIX protocol document, RFC 5101.
sections.eli5: Reports that show bits of real packets can reveal private things. So they may only show the top of the packet, never everything, and the report has to travel in a locked box.

sections.title: Numbering and the Registry
sections.content:
The model has two sets of assigned numbers. For general IPFIX numbers, RFC 5102 applies. The PSAMP Information Element IDs were deliberately started at 301 to leave a gap for ongoing IPFIX work, and the RFC expects IANA to fill that gap with new IPFIX elements.

The initial content of the selectorAlgorithm registry is in Section 8.2.1. New assignments are made by IANA after Expert Review, once a specification of the new method and any new Information Elements is provided. The experts will initially be drawn from the Working Group Chairs and document editors of the IPFIX and PSAMP Working Groups.
sections.eli5: The new words got numbers starting at 301 so there was still room in the older list for its own new words. A small panel of experts approves new picking methods.
